label: Government levels
quiz: What should a learner identify when studying an alcalde mayor or corregidor?
The office's jurisdiction and historical period
An identical modern office in all cases
retry: Which statement distinguishes a government chart from evidence of effects?
A chart describes relationships; implementation needs further evidence
A chart proves universal consent
Every arrow guarantees success
A title reveals all consequences
hard: A diagram shows an order moving between levels but no action record. What remains unknown?
How it was implemented and how people responded
Whether the diagram contains labels
Whether central offices can be studied
Whether a source needs a date

label: Town office
quiz: Which office was town-level rather than the central governor-general?
retry: Why should colonial town selection not be equated automatically with modern elections?
Rules and participation need their own historical context
All periods used identical rules
Every resident necessarily participated equally
No historical evidence can be used
hard: A caption says a gobernadorcillo personally governed every island. What correction fits?
Identify the town-level role and distinguish the central office
Keep it because all titles mean the same role
Call every resident a governor-general
Use a modern election claim without evidence

label: Leadership and change
quiz: What does continuity mean in comparing local leadership?
Something carried on while other relationships could change
retry: Why should principales not be treated as every Indigenous person?
The term concerns prominent local participants, not the whole population
Every community had one identical social experience
An elite title reveals all residents' wishes
Local people had no history before offices
hard: A family retained influence while holding a new office. Which comparison is careful?
Identify continuity of influence and change of institutional setting
Say nothing changed in any respect
Say all earlier local influence vanished
Apply that family's experience to everyone

label: Intermediaries and requests
quiz: What does an intermediary do in this lesson?
Connects institutions and communities through information or demands
retry: What does a petition establish most directly?
A formal request was made, not necessarily granted
Every resident agreed and the request succeeded
No local person acted
The complete effects of every policy
hard: A request for relief has no recorded reply. What should a report say?
Describe the request and leave its outcome open pending evidence
Declare success because it was requested
Invent an approving official reply
Treat silence as every household's consent

label: Checking local records
quiz: Why does an official roster not prove fair government?
It names positions or holders, not all actions and outcomes
No person can be named in a record
retry: Which question helps check representation in a petition?
Whose voices appear and whose views remain missing?
Why must all residents have identical interests?
Which invented speech will fill all gaps?
Why should context be ignored?
hard: An official and a household account emphasize different experiences. What should a learner do?
Compare their purposes, actions described and supporting evidence
Reject the household account solely because it is unofficial
Assume both writers knew every private thought
Treat the office title as a substitute for evidence
